Cc: Evan Li <evan.li@fastrail.com>

Subject: Redwood MSA redlines — indemnity and third-party IP

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and legal at FastRail reviewed the MSA and pushed back primarily on the indemnity section for third-party IP claims. We've attached our annotated redlines and an evidence matrix showing what we can reasonably provide if a claim arises.

High-level asks from our side:
- FastRail needs either (A) the right to control defense for third-party IP claims that arise from our supplied data or (B) a clear reimbursement pathway if Redwood defends and settles.
- A threshold for escrow activation: procurement wants an evidentiary threshold (e.g., demonstrable technical linkage + claim notice window) before escrow funds can be drawn.
- A narrow carveout for open-source components we supply — we can provide SBOMs but won't indemnify Redwood for downstream OSS claims.

We're flexible on cap negotiation, but we need an operational workflow for evidence requests (timelines, point-of-contact, privileged communications). Can your legal team propose concrete changes rather than a purely legal principle? Procurement is on a compressed timeline and prefers a short call early next week.

Attachments: FastRail_MSA_redlines_20260925.pdf, FastRail_evidence_matrix_20260925.xlsx

Thanks,
Maya Chopra

Subject: Re: Redwood MSA redlines — indemnity and third-party IP

Sean/Laura — thanks for the ping and to Maya/Evan for the redlines. I read FastRail's annotations and prepared a pragmatic compromise; high level first, then specific language bullets.

High-level strawman (proposal we can take to FastRail):
1) Defense control: Redwood will retain the right to defend third-party IP claims that arise solely from Redwood's model or runtime. FastRail may assume control of defense if Redwood declines to defend within 14 days of written notice. This preserves Redwood's ability to manage settlement strategy while giving the customer a clear fallback.
2) Reimbursement option: If FastRail assumes defense, Redwood will reimburse reasonable, documented defense costs up to the indemnity cap. Reimbursement excludes FastRail's internal personnel time (standard).
3) Escrow activation & evidence threshold: Escrow can be accessed only after (a) FastRail provides a written claim notice with purported claim documents and (b) Redwood's counsel confirms a plausible linkage between the claim and the covered product within a 10-business-day review window. If linkage is disputed, funds are held pending neutral escrow arbiter review.
4) OSS carveout: FastRail will not be required to indemnify Redwood for claims arising from OSS components listed on SBOMs the customer provides, except where FastRail modified OSS and redistributed it to Redwood in a manner inconsistent with upstream licenses.
5) Cap structure: propose a sliding cap tied to committed annual spend (e.g., 3x ARR for standard, negotiable upward for enterprise). We can include an exception for IP indemnity arising from Gross Negligence or Willful Misconduct.

Suggested redline snippets (plain English to be turned into clause language):
- "Redwood shall have the initial right, but not the obligation, to assume the defense of any third-party claim alleging infringement. Customer may assume defense 14 days after written notice if Redwood fails to do so."
- "Escrow release shall require: (i) Customer's written claim notice with supporting documents; and (ii) verification by Redwood counsel of a plausible technical linkage within 10 business days. If counsel cannot verify linkage within 10 business days, parties shall submit the dispute to the escrow agent for resolution and funds shall remain in escrow until resolution."

Operational asks we need from FastRail to make this work:
- Primary technical contact and SOC point for evidence requests (name, email, SLA for evidence delivery).
- Which SBOM format (CycloneDX or SPDX) they will deliver and cadence for updates.
- Whether procurement requires escrow agent identity or can accept a Redwood-approved agent (we typically use IronHold Escrow Services).

I'll draft formal clause text after we confirm the customer's tolerance for the cap and whether they insist on defense control as the first option.

Kimberly Park
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

On Mon, Sep 28, 2026 at 8:16 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sean/Laura — thanks for the ping and to Maya/Evan for the redlines. I read FastRail's annotations and prepared a pragmatic compromise; high level first, then specific language bullets.

Kimberly — this is helpful and closer to what procurement needs. A few clarifications from FastRail:
- The 14-day assumption window for defense is acceptable, but procurement insists that if FastRail assumes defense we retain the right to select outside counsel (subject to Redwood's reasonable objection).
- Regarding the 10-business-day linkage review: we can comply with a 10-business-day window for initial plausibility. If Redwood's counsel requests specific logs or artifacts beyond what FastRail has in the attached evidence matrix, we need a 5-business-day SLA to collect and deliver those artifacts.
- SBOM: FastRail will provide CycloneDX, updated quarterly.
- Escrow agent: procurement prefers a neutral third-party; IronHold is OK provided FastRail has veto power over agent selection for the specific engagement.

We have one additional constraint: FastRail's procurement team cannot accept an indemnity cap that is lower than the committed annual spend x2 for strategic vendors; that's their internal policy. They'll relax the multiplier for smaller pilots but not for production contracts.

We can take the strawman language to procurement tomorrow. Monday 10am PT works for our team for a 30-minute call.

Thanks,
Maya
